title: Note: reading a ghost story, part 1
summary: The first sentences of an original ghost story, read with the structure from the earlier lessons: a sentence that ends in a noun, and one very long describer.

blocks.text: This is a guided reading of a short ghost story (怪談) written for FluRai. Instead of teaching a new rule, it shows how to approach real material: stop at every sentence and ask what it is made of. The story continues over three notes. Here are its first sentences.

blocks.jp: それは、美咲が友達の家の鍋パーティーに参加した、雪の夜。
blocks.en: It was the snowy night when Misaki took part in the hot-pot party at her friend's house.

blocks.jp: パーティーが終わると、美咲は一人で駅へ向かった。
blocks.en: When the party ended, Misaki set out for the station alone.

blocks.jp: 雪が静かに降っていた。
道の先に、古くて小さな家があった。
blocks.en: Ahead on the road there was an old, small house.

blocks.jp: 窓の中に、白い顔があった。
blocks.en: In the window there was a white face.

blocks.text: A sentence that ends in a noun

The first sentence ends on a bare noun, 雪の夜. A noun at the end is an A-is-B sentence with the copula だ dropped, which is common in casual narration. So それは … 雪の夜 is "It was the snowy night ...". (それ is "that": it points at something the listener is about to learn.)

Everything between それは and 夜 is one long describer. It has its own carriage, 美咲が, and its own engine, 参加した. But the engine is inside a describer, and it stands in front of a noun. So the whole stretch only tells you which night.

cars.text: 美咲が友達の家の鍋パーティーに参加した
cars.label: one long describer

blocks.text: それは、美咲が友達の家の鍋パーティーに参加した、雪の夜。 The describer hangs on 夜.
When you meet a long sentence, look at its end first. Here it ends in a noun, so everything before it describes that noun. Read the rest backwards from there.

items: Work through the story one sentence at a time.
A sentence can end in a bare noun: the copula だ is dropped.
A long stretch in front of a noun is one describer, even when it holds its own carriage and engine.
Listen first, then analyze, then listen again.
